summary: Replayed the merged managed BuildKit and artifact-cache convergence on the docker-build VM, bootstrapped the remote builder, and verified the private cache endpoints from build and runtime consumers.

verification.observed: Ansible recap was ok=157 changed=1 unreachable=0 failed=0; 0mcp-buildkitd.service is active and enabled, the legacy unit is inactive and disabled, obsolete containers are absent, and the persistent cache path is present.
The mcp-cache builder bootstrapped on BuildKit 0.33.1 with a linux/amd64 worker; a local-only OCI amd64 canary built successfully and the temporary artifact was removed.
The /v2/ endpoints on ports 5001-5004 responded from both docker-build and docker-runtime. Monitoring access remained a separate pending firewall repair.

notes: Restic snapshot metadata advanced after the live apply; the retained evidence confirms the manifest update, not a separately captured wrapper exit code.

The pre-apply idle check found no active CI/build jobs, but the apply-lock context was released before the make process ran. No overlap was observed; this deviation remains visible, and future mutation subprocesses must hold the lock for their entire duration.
